A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOBOLFI research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, and appendices A–D. Corresponding material can be matched despite reformatting, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original simulation comparisons, MLBA posterior estimates for the electric-vehicle preference survey, and supplementary sensitivity and bacterial-transmission experiments.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds BOLFI comparisons in the real-data and misspecified-MLBA experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Appendix A retain the discrepancy-vector construction, Gaussian-process surrogate, correlated noise, NEHVI acquisition, likelihood approximations, and scaling algorithm. The expanded covariance and scalability discussion explains the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the Gaussian/Brownian-motion examples, synthetic and misspecified MLBA, the same survey with 149 participants and 584 observations, and the day-care transmission example. The misspecified MLBA scenario already appears in v3 Appendix C.3.1.

E2.justification: V4 adds joint-data BOLFI to the real-data posterior comparison, previously limited to MOBOLFI and the closed-form reference. It also adds RT-only and choice-only BOLFI acquisition comparisons to the retained misspecified-MLBA experiment in Figure 6.

E3.justification: The added real-data BOLFI evaluation uses summed log-discrepancies, the 282-point initialization, and the 50-replicate discrepancy construction, with training iterations matched to MOBOLFI. V4 also introduces single-source acquisition controls for the existing conflict experiment; the previously reported experimental settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: V4 Figure 6 extends the existing misspecification analysis by comparing how MOBOLFI and single-source BOLFI explore conflicting likelihood regions. The scaling, tolerance, iteration-count, auxiliary-summary, and source-specific-parameter analyses were already present in v3.

E5.justification: The posterior-uncertainty reporting and disclosed simulation and MCMC counts are retained, including Appendix B.1 and C.2 settings and the 1,000-replicate discrepancy histograms. No new seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: V4 Figure 7 newly reports BOLFI posterior curves and means for the real data, showing poorer agreement with the closed-form reference than MOBOLFI. Figure 6 adds BOLFI acquisition clouds and their contrasting exploration pattern. These extend results within retained settings, while the principal earlier findings remain.

T1.justification: The likelihood, Gaussian-process, and Pareto definitions and the appendix derivations are retained apart from notation and numbering edits. The glossary restates existing definitions; the new discussion of published theoretical guarantees supplies context and limitations without adding a formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain simulation-efficient approximation of joint and individual-source likelihoods, avoiding problematic scalar discrepancy combinations, and diagnosing conflicting information. The rewritten abstract and emphasis on single-run exploration clarify capabilities already described in v3.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands interpretation and limitations: Sections 3.2–3.3 discuss missing NEHVI convergence guarantees, dependence modeling, and circumstances where many-source computational overhead could favor BOLFI. Section 4.2.4 distinguishes discrepancy, tolerance, surrogate, and noise-model errors. The misspecification discussion also replaces v3's claim of acquiring all local optima with a qualified description of observed exploration.

D1.justification: V4 documents the new real-data BOLFI target and training-data construction and includes it in the stated posterior-sampling procedure. The existing code-access statements and the detailed implementation and hyperparameter information in the appendices are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds Li and Fearnhead (2018) and Zhang and Golovin (2020), connecting the work to ABC distance scaling and optimization guarantees. The broader related-work discussion remains stable; publication-metadata updates and duplicate-reference cleanup do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: V4 rewrites the abstract and selected explanatory paragraphs, adds glossary guidance, and moves scaling and misspecified-MLBA material into the main text. The overall section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 extensively reformats the document and redraws most plots with revised typography, axes, gridlines, legends, and colors, replacing many low-resolution embedded plots with vector graphics. It relocates the scaling and misspecification figures, adds BOLFI displays, and introduces the notation glossary as Table 1.

improvement.justification: The added real-data BOLFI comparison and conflict-exploration controls strengthen empirical support for the retained contributions. More explicit approximation errors, computational limits, and qualifications improve the interpretation of the evidence, while clearer figures and the glossary aid reading. Together these provide a supported, incremental improvement to the existing study.
